# AWS EBS CSI Driver Health Check
#
# Validates that the AWS EBS CSI Driver is running and healthy in the
# kube-system namespace. Checks that the ebs-csi-controller deployment has
# at least one available replica and that no EBS CSI driver pods (selected
# by label) are stuck in Pending, Failed, or Unknown phases. Label selectors
# are used because kube-system is a shared namespace.
apiVersion: chainsaw.kyverno.io/v1alpha1
kind: Test
metadata:
  name: aws-ebs-csi-driver-health-check
spec:
  timeouts:
    assert: 5m
  steps:
    - name: validate-deployment-exists
      try:
        # Guard against vacuous pass: verify the ebs-csi-controller
        # deployment exists and has at least one ready replica.
        - assert:
            resource:
              apiVersion: apps/v1
              kind: Deployment
              metadata:
                name: ebs-csi-controller
                namespace: kube-system
              status:
                (availableReplicas > `0`): true
    - name: validate-all-pods-healthy
      try:
        # Assert no EBS CSI driver pods are in unhealthy phases
        # (Pending / Failed / Unknown) or stuck in Running phase
        # with a known-bad container-waiting reason
        # (CrashLoopBackOff, ImagePullBackOff, ErrImagePull,
        # CreateContainerConfigError). Phase-only filtering misses
        # CrashLoopBackOff because such pods typically remain in
        # Running phase with an unhealthy container.
        # Uses label selector because kube-system is a shared namespace.
        - error:
            resource:
              apiVersion: v1
              kind: Pod
              metadata:
                namespace: kube-system
                labels:
                  app.kubernetes.io/name: aws-ebs-csi-driver
              status:
                phase: Pending
        - error:
            resource:
              apiVersion: v1
              kind: Pod
              metadata:
                namespace: kube-system
                labels:
                  app.kubernetes.io/name: aws-ebs-csi-driver
              status:
                phase: Failed
        - error:
            resource:
              apiVersion: v1
              kind: Pod
              metadata:
                namespace: kube-system
                labels:
                  app.kubernetes.io/name: aws-ebs-csi-driver
              status:
                phase: Unknown
        # JMESPath projection (not single-element match): kyverno-json's
        # sliceNode.Assert gates on exact slice length before per-element
        # comparison, so a `containerStatuses: - state: ...` shape only
        # matches single-container pods and silently passes sidecars. Use
        # `containerStatuses[?...] | length(@) > 0` to fire on any
        # container at any index. Parallel initContainerStatuses block
        # below catches init-container failures (invisible to
        # containerStatuses). Per PR #1245 review (@ArangoGutierrez).
        - error:
            resource:
              apiVersion: v1
              kind: Pod
              metadata:
                namespace: kube-system
                labels:
                  app.kubernetes.io/name: aws-ebs-csi-driver
              status:
                ((containerStatuses || `[]`)[?state.waiting.reason == 'CrashLoopBackOff' || state.waiting.reason == 'ImagePullBackOff' || state.waiting.reason == 'ErrImagePull' || state.waiting.reason == 'CreateContainerConfigError'] | length(@) > `0`): true
        - error:
            resource:
              apiVersion: v1
              kind: Pod
              metadata:
                namespace: kube-system
                labels:
                  app.kubernetes.io/name: aws-ebs-csi-driver
              status:
                ((initContainerStatuses || `[]`)[?state.waiting.reason == 'CrashLoopBackOff' || state.waiting.reason == 'ImagePullBackOff' || state.waiting.reason == 'ErrImagePull' || state.waiting.reason == 'CreateContainerConfigError'] | length(@) > `0`): true

# ErrImagePull, CreateContainerConfigError) are label-scoped because
# kube-system is a shared namespace.

# Cert Manager Health Check
#
# Validates that cert-manager is running and healthy in the cert-manager
# namespace. The chart deploys three Deployments — the controller
# (cert-manager), the CA injector (cert-manager-cainjector), and the
# webhook (cert-manager-webhook) — all of which must be available for
# the operator to issue / inject / validate certificates. The previous
# check only asserted the controller; this check covers all three to
# avoid silently passing while the webhook is down (which would block
# every Certificate/Issuer CR admission).
#
# Also asserts the three core CRDs are Established=True so the
# apiserver will accept CRs of those kinds (per #1222 / #660).
apiVersion: chainsaw.kyverno.io/v1alpha1
kind: Test
metadata:
  name: cert-manager-health-check
spec:
  timeouts:
    assert: 5m
  steps:
    - name: validate-crds-established
      try:
        - assert:
            resource:
              apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
              kind: CustomResourceDefinition
              metadata:
                name: certificates.cert-manager.io
              status:
                (conditions[?type == 'Established']):
                  - status: "True"
        - assert:
            resource:
              apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
              kind: CustomResourceDefinition
              metadata:
                name: issuers.cert-manager.io
              status:
                (conditions[?type == 'Established']):
                  - status: "True"
        - assert:
            resource:
              apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
              kind: CustomResourceDefinition
              metadata:
                name: clusterissuers.cert-manager.io
              status:
                (conditions[?type == 'Established']):
                  - status: "True"
    - name: validate-controller-deployment
      try:
        - assert:
            resource:
              apiVersion: apps/v1
              kind: Deployment
              metadata:
                name: cert-manager
                namespace: cert-manager
              status:
                (availableReplicas > `0`): true
    - name: validate-cainjector-deployment
      try:
        - assert:
            resource:
              apiVersion: apps/v1
              kind: Deployment
              metadata:
                name: cert-manager-cainjector
                namespace: cert-manager

                (availableReplicas > `0`): true

        - error:
            resource:
              apiVersion: v1
              kind: Pod
              metadata:
                namespace: cert-manager
              status:
                phase: Pending
        - error:
            resource:
              apiVersion: v1
              kind: Pod
              metadata:
                namespace: cert-manager
              status:
                phase: Failed
        - error:
            resource:
              apiVersion: v1
              kind: Pod
              metadata:
                namespace: cert-manager
              status:
                phase: Unknown

        # sliceNode.Assert gates on exact slice length before per-element
        # comparison, so a `containerStatuses: - state: ...` shape only
        # matches single-container pods and silently passes sidecars. Use
        # `containerStatuses[?...] | length(@) > 0` to fire on any
        # container at any index. Parallel initContainerStatuses block
        # below catches init-container failures (invisible to
        # containerStatuses). Per PR #1245 review (@ArangoGutierrez).
        - error:
            resource:
              apiVersion: v1
              kind: Pod
              metadata:
                namespace: cert-manager
              status:
                ((containerStatuses || `[]`)[?state.waiting.reason == 'CrashLoopBackOff' || state.waiting.reason == 'ImagePullBackOff' || state.waiting.reason == 'ErrImagePull' || state.waiting.reason == 'CreateContainerConfigError'] | length(@) > `0`): true

# dra-node-labeler health check.
#
# The labeler mirrors nvidia.com/gpu.present onto the DRA eviction label the
# kubelet plugin selects on. A labeler that never starts takes the kubelet
# plugin to DESIRED=0 and removes every ResourceSlice, so the DaemonSet must
# roll out fully: updatedNumberScheduled == desiredNumberScheduled, with
# desiredNumberScheduled > 0 as a guard against a vacuous pass when no node
# carries gpu.present yet. A pod that restarts (RunContainerError, a script
# that exits non-zero) fails the pod assertion.
apiVersion: chainsaw.kyverno.io/v1alpha1
kind: Test
metadata:
  name: dra-node-labeler-health-check
spec:
  timeouts:
    assert: 5m
  steps:
    - name: validate-daemonset-fully-rolled-out
      try:
        - assert:
            resource:
              apiVersion: apps/v1
              kind: DaemonSet
              metadata:
                name: dra-node-labeler
                namespace: gpu-operator
              status:
                (desiredNumberScheduled > `0`): true
                (updatedNumberScheduled == desiredNumberScheduled): true
                (numberReady == desiredNumberScheduled): true
    - name: validate-pods-healthy
      try:
        - assert:
            resource:
              apiVersion: v1

# GPU Operator Health Check
#
# Validates the GPU operator stack:
# 1. The gpu-operator Deployment has at least one available replica.
# 2. The clusterpolicies.nvidia.com CRD is Established (apiserver will
#    accept the singleton ClusterPolicy CR).
# 3. The ClusterPolicy singleton named "cluster-policy" has reconciled
#    to status.state == "ready" — this is the deepest signal that the
#    full GPU stack (driver, toolkit, cuda, plugin DaemonSets, validators)
#    is healthy. Migrates the verifyClusterPolicyReady Go check that
#    PR #1235 task 7 deferred for assertion-equivalence proof.
# 4. No pods in unhealthy phases or stuck container-waiting states.
#
# The nvidia-operator-validator DaemonSet runs 4 sequential init
# containers (driver, toolkit, cuda, plugin) before reaching Running;
# the ClusterPolicy state assertion is the canonical post-reconcile
# signal that all four passed.

metadata:
  name: gpu-operator-health-check
spec:
  timeouts:
    assert: 5m
  steps:
    - name: validate-cluster-policy-crd-established
      try:
        - assert:
            resource:
              apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
              kind: CustomResourceDefinition
              metadata:
                name: clusterpolicies.nvidia.com
              status:
                (conditions[?type == 'Established']):
                  - status: "True"
    - name: validate-deployment-exists
      try:
        # Guard against vacuous pass on empty namespace: verify the
        # gpu-operator deployment exists and has at least one ready replica.
        - assert:
            resource:
              apiVersion: apps/v1

              metadata:

                namespace: gpu-operator

              metadata:
                name: cluster-policy
              status:
                state: ready

        # below catches init-container failures (invisible to

#    vacuous-pass guard so a missing StatefulSet does not silently pass.
# 5. The Alertmanager StatefulSet (alertmanager-kube-prometheus-alertmanager)
#    reaches the same full-rollout threshold.

#    kube-prometheus-stack) are stuck in Pending, Failed, Unknown, or a
#    known-bad container-waiting reason (CrashLoopBackOff, ImagePullBackOff,
#    ErrImagePull, CreateContainerConfigError).

# in recipes/components/kube-prometheus-stack/values.yaml. The prometheus-
# operator creates StatefulSets named <workload>-<cr-name>, and the chart
# renders CR names as <fullname>-<workload>. Names verified against
# tests/chainsaw/ai-conformance/common/assert-monitoring.yaml and
# tests/chainsaw/ai-conformance/kind-common/assert-monitoring.yaml

#
# Validates the standalone NFD deployment by checking:
# 1. NFD Master Deployment has at least one ready replica
# 2. NFD Worker DaemonSet has fully rolled out and is current
#    (desiredNumberScheduled > 0, numberReady/updatedNumberScheduled both
#    match it, and observedGeneration matches metadata.generation, so
#    neither a partial nor a stale rollout passes)
# 3. NFD GC Deployment has at least one ready replica (gc.enable: true)
#
# Resource names: AICR deploys the kubernetes-sigs/node-feature-discovery
# chart under release name "nfd" (matching the ComponentRef Name in
# recipes/registry.yaml). The chart's fullname template prefixes the
# release name to the chart name when they don't overlap, yielding
# "nfd-node-feature-discovery-*" for the master Deployment, worker
# DaemonSet, and gc Deployment. If a deployer ever switches the release
# name to "node-feature-discovery", these asserts need updating in
# lockstep.
# 4. No pods in unhealthy phases (Pending, Failed, Unknown) or stuck in
#    Running with a known-unhealthy container waiting reason
#    (CrashLoopBackOff, ImagePullBackOff, ErrImagePull,
#    CreateContainerConfigError)

kind: Test
metadata:
  name: nfd-health-check
spec:
  timeouts:
    assert: 5m
  steps:
    - name: validate-master-deployment
      try:
        - assert:
            resource:
              apiVersion: apps/v1
              kind: Deployment
              metadata:
                name: nfd-node-feature-discovery-master
                namespace: node-feature-discovery
              status:
                (availableReplicas > `0`): true

      try:
        - assert:
            resource:
              apiVersion: apps/v1
              kind: DaemonSet
              metadata:

                namespace: node-feature-discovery

              # DaemonSet: require at least one scheduled pod.
              ((status.desiredNumberScheduled || `0`) > `0`): true

              # the guard above, this rejects partial failures. We assert on
              # numberReady (always present in DaemonSetStatus) rather than
              # numberUnavailable, which is `omitempty` and disappears from
              # the status when zero — making `numberUnavailable == 0`
              # evaluate `null == 0` (false) on a fully-healthy DaemonSet.

              # previous revision (also Ready) from a fully current rollout;

# Nodewright Customizations Health Check
#
# Validates that the NodeWright custom resource(s) deployed by the nodewright-customizations
# component have completed successfully. The NodeWright CR status.status (see
# github.com/NVIDIA/nodewright/chart/templates/nodewright-crd.yaml) is one of: unknown,
# complete, blocked, waiting, disabled, paused, in_progress, erroring. This check
# asserts status.status is "complete" so that node-level customizations (e.g. tuning)
# have been applied to all matching nodes.
#
# Kind (#2593): nodewright-operator v0.18.0 renamed
# skyhook.nvidia.com Skyhook to nodewright.nvidia.com NodeWright. The operator
# mirrors each legacy Skyhook into a NodeWright and writes status ONLY on the
# NodeWright, so asserting the legacy kind never sees "complete" even on a fully
# tuned cluster. The manifests may still declare Skyhook; the mirrored NodeWright
# of the same name is what carries the status. A static assert cannot fall back,
# so this check follows the pinned operator. When the recipe pins the operator
# below v0.18.0 and the cluster serves only skyhook.nvidia.com, the deployment
# validator skips this assert (gatedHealthCheckSuppressed) and the Go readiness
# check verifies the Skyhook CRs by name instead, so a healthy legacy cluster
# still passes. A v0.18.0+ pin on a cluster that does not serve
# nodewright.nvidia.com fails closed: that is a broken operator install, and a
# stale legacy Skyhook must not stand in for the missing NodeWright.
#
# Value-gate awareness (#1844): this static assert cannot see the component's
# effective Helm values, so it would fail when the whole `tuning` CR is
# deliberately suppressed — e.g. `--set nodewrightcustomizations:tuningEnabled=false`
# on a single-package tuning manifest (tuning-gke.yaml / tuning-generic.yaml). The
# deployment validator therefore renders the component's manifests with the
# effective values and skips this assert when they yield no Nodewright CR (see
# nodewrightHealthCheckSuppressed in validators/deployment/expected_resources.go).
# The skip is fail-closed: whenever the values keep the CR, the render still lists
# it and this assert runs — only an intentionally-absent CR is tolerated. The
# render-aware Go readiness check (verifyNodewrightReady) enforces the same
# status.status == "complete" signal (plus the runtime-required taint gate), so
# nodewright readiness is never left unverified.
#
# Boundary: the suppression must be in the recipe (an overlay-declared or inline
# `overrides:`, e.g. the AKS tuningEnabled: false default), because the in-cluster
# validator Job renders from the recipe it is handed. A bundle-time-only
# `--set` is NOT persisted to the recipe and `aicr validate` has no `--set`, so
# it does not reach this render. See docs/contributor/validator.md
# ("Value-gate awareness").
apiVersion: chainsaw.kyverno.io/v1alpha1
kind: Test
metadata:
  name: nodewright-customizations-health-check
spec:
  timeouts:
    assert: 5m
  steps:
    - name: validate-nodewright-cr-complete
      try:
        # Assert a NodeWright CR has status.status == "complete" per the
        # NodeWright CRD schema. NodeWright is cluster-scoped.
        #
        # Deliberately name-agnostic. The manifests do not agree on a name —
        # tuning.yaml / tuning-gke.yaml / tuning-generic.yaml render "tuning"
        # while no-op.yaml renders "no-op" — so a hardcoded name asserts a CR
        # that never exists for any component wiring a differently-named
        # manifest. A nameless assert uses the executor's list-and-match path
        # (pkg/chainsaw/inprocess.go): it fails closed when the collection is
        # empty (ErrCodeNotFound, not a vacuous pass) and passes when a live,
        # non-terminating NodeWright reports complete.
        #
        # Per-CR completeness is not weakened by this: the render-aware Go
        # readiness check (verifyNodewrightReady) derives the expected CR names
        # from the component's rendered manifests and requires every one of
        # them to be live (not Terminating) and complete, reporting each failure
        # by name. That per-name gate is what binds readiness to the CRs the
        # recipe declared — this assert alone would accept a stale or unrelated
        # complete NodeWright.
        - assert:
            resource:
              apiVersion: nodewright.nvidia.com/v1alpha1
              kind: NodeWright
              status:
                status: complete

# Validates that the Nodewright Operator is running and healthy in the
# skyhook namespace:
# 1. skyhooks.skyhook.nvidia.com CRD Established=True (the apiserver
#    will accept Skyhook CRs that nodewright-customizations declares).

#    nodewrights.nodewright.nvidia.com CRD is deliberately not asserted
#    here so a v0.17.x operator still passes. The Go readiness gate
#    (resolveNodewrightGVR) fails closed when the recipe pins v0.18.0+ and
#    that group is not served, so its absence is never mistaken for a
#    legacy operator.
# 2. skyhook-operator-controller-manager Deployment has at least one
#    available replica.
# 3. No pods stuck in Pending/Failed/Unknown phases or known-bad
#    container-waiting states.

kind: Test
metadata:
  name: nodewright-operator-health-check
spec:
  timeouts:
    assert: 5m
  steps:
    - name: validate-skyhook-crd-established
      try:
        - assert:
            resource:
              apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
              kind: CustomResourceDefinition
              metadata:
                name: skyhooks.skyhook.nvidia.com
              status:
                (conditions[?type == 'Established']):
                  - status: "True"
    - name: validate-deployment-exists
      try:
        - assert:
            resource:
              apiVersion: apps/v1
              kind: Deployment
              metadata:
                name: skyhook-operator-controller-manager
                namespace: nodewright
              status:
                (availableReplicas > `0`): true
    - name: validate-all-pods-healthy
      try:
        - error:
            resource:
              apiVersion: v1
              kind: Pod
              metadata:
                namespace: nodewright
              status:
                phase: Pending
        - error:
            resource:
              apiVersion: v1
              kind: Pod
              metadata:
                namespace: nodewright
              status:
                phase: Failed
        - error:
            resource:
              apiVersion: v1
              kind: Pod
              metadata:
                namespace: nodewright
              status:
                phase: Unknown

        # sliceNode.Assert gates on exact slice length before per-element
        # comparison, so a `containerStatuses: - state: ...` shape only
        # matches single-container pods and silently passes sidecars. Use

        # container at any index. Parallel initContainerStatuses block

              apiVersion: v1
              kind: Pod
              metadata:
                namespace: nodewright
              status:

# NVSentinel Health Check
#
# Validates that NVSentinel is running and healthy in the nvsentinel
# namespace. Checks that the labeler deployment has at least one
# available replica, that the required DaemonSets gated on the labeler's
# driver.installed node label (metadata-collector,
# syslog-health-monitor-regular; the optional syslog-health-monitor-kata
# legitimately has 0 desired without Kata nodes and is excluded) are
# actually rolled out, and that no pods
# in the namespace are stuck in Pending, Failed, or Unknown phases.
apiVersion: chainsaw.kyverno.io/v1alpha1
kind: Test
metadata:
  name: nvsentinel-health-check
spec:
  # 90s, deliberately below the 5m the sibling checks author. The
  # in-process executor (pkg/chainsaw/inprocess.go) supports exactly one
  # timeout knob — this Test-level assert budget caps the WHOLE check
  # (per-step/per-operation timeouts are not honored) — and this check is
  # uniquely prone to a legitimately-never-true wait: on a cluster in the
  # #2175 broken state the driver-labeled DaemonSets sit at 0 desired
  # FOREVER, so a 5m budget here does not buy readiness, it buys a stall.
  # Verified live (issue #2186): the stalled assert pushed the
  # expected-resources Job past its 8m activeDeadline, the pod was
  # deleted, and the operator saw "pod not found" (status=other) instead
  # of the assert diff naming the DaemonSets. 90s fails fast with the
  # real message while still covering the healthy path, where every step
  # passes in seconds (the components are already rolled out by the time
  # the deployment phase runs).
  timeouts:
    assert: 90s
  steps:
    - name: validate-deployment-exists
      try:
        # Guard against vacuous pass on empty namespace: verify the
        # nvsentinel-controller-manager deployment exists and has at least
        # one ready replica.
        - assert:
            resource:
              apiVersion: apps/v1
              kind: Deployment
              metadata:
                name: labeler
                namespace: nvsentinel
              status:
                (availableReplicas > `0`): true
    - name: validate-driver-labeled-daemonsets-rolled-out
      try:
        # metadata-collector and syslog-health-monitor-regular select on
        # the nvsentinel.dgxc.nvidia.com/driver.installed node label, which
        # the labeler applies only when it can observe a GPU driver pod.
        # Where the driver ships in the node image (AKS azure-managed, GKE
        # COS gke-default, OKE) the label is never applied and both
        # DaemonSets sit at 0 desired pods. That state is invisible to the
        # assertions in the surrounding steps: pods that are never created
        # cannot be Pending, Failed, or CrashLooping, and the labeler
        # Deployment itself stays available — which is how issue #2175
        # shipped unnoticed.
        #
        # Assert non-omitempty status fields only. numberUnavailable is
        # omitempty, so it is ABSENT on a healthy DaemonSet and a
        # `numberUnavailable: 0` assertion passes vacuously on a 0-desired
        # DaemonSet too. desiredNumberScheduled and numberReady are always
        # serialized, so the pair below fails closed on 0 desired.
        #
        # syslog-health-monitor-kata and gpu-health-monitor-dcgm-3.x are
        # deliberately NOT asserted: both legitimately have 0 desired pods
        # on clusters without Kata nodes / DCGM 3.x GPUs.
        # metadata-collector uses the NEGATIVE (error-op) form, not a
        # positive assert: the bundle-time RuntimeClass gate explicitly
        # permits disabling the subchart (global.metadataCollector.enabled
        # =false renders no DaemonSet), so a positive existence assert
        # would fail deployment validation for a configuration bundling
        # explicitly allows. The error ops below pass on a true 404
        # (disabled subchart — the in-process executor fails closed on
        # transient fetch errors, so this is not an API-blip loophole)
        # while still catching both failure states when the DaemonSet IS
        # rendered: the #2175 signature (present with 0 desired) and a
        # partial rollout. Trade-off, stated plainly: a DaemonSet deleted
        # out-of-band also passes — accepted, because the disabled-
        # subchart configuration is supported and chainsaw cannot
        # condition one resource's assert on another's values.
        - error:
            resource:
              apiVersion: apps/v1
              kind: DaemonSet
              metadata:
                name: metadata-collector
                namespace: nvsentinel
              status:
                # `> `0`: false` rather than `== `0`: true`: kyverno-json's
                # equality between an int64 field (what unstructured cluster
                # reads and the in-process fetcher both deliver) and a JMESPath
                # numeric literal is type-strict and never matches, so the ==
                # form silently disarms this op. The ordering comparator
                # coerces numeric kinds and is already relied on by the assert
                # ops below; expecting false inverts it into "desired is zero".
                (desiredNumberScheduled > `0`): false
        - error:
            resource:
              apiVersion: apps/v1
              kind: DaemonSet
              metadata:
                name: metadata-collector
                namespace: nvsentinel
              status:
                (numberReady < desiredNumberScheduled): true
        # Stale-rollout guard: numberReady alone can't distinguish a node
        # still running the previous revision's pod (also Ready) from a
        # fully current rollout. Flat (not status:-nested) so
        # metadata.generation is addressable below. `<` (not `!=`) states
        # the violated invariant directly: fewer nodes updated than desired.
        # updatedNumberScheduled is itself omitempty (unlike
        # desiredNumberScheduled/numberReady), so it needs the `|| `0``
        # null-coalescing too.
        - error:
            resource:
              apiVersion: apps/v1
              kind: DaemonSet
              metadata:
                name: metadata-collector
                namespace: nvsentinel
              ((status.updatedNumberScheduled || `0`) < status.desiredNumberScheduled): true
        - error:
            resource:
              apiVersion: apps/v1
              kind: DaemonSet
              metadata:
                name: metadata-collector
                namespace: nvsentinel
              ((status.observedGeneration || `0`) < metadata.generation): true
        # syslog-health-monitor-regular: same negative form — the
        # syslog-health-monitor subchart is switchable via its chart
        # condition (global.syslogHealthMonitor.enabled) exactly like
        # metadata-collector, and the driver-label gate's consumer-aware
        # skip treats it as an optional label consumer, so the one
        # coherent rule is "explicitly-disabled consumers render nothing
        # and validation tolerates their absence; rendered consumers must
        # be fully rolled out".
        - error:
            resource:
              apiVersion: apps/v1
              kind: DaemonSet
              metadata:
                name: syslog-health-monitor-regular
                namespace: nvsentinel
              status:
                (desiredNumberScheduled > `0`): false
        - error:
            resource:
              apiVersion: apps/v1
              kind: DaemonSet
              metadata:
                name: syslog-health-monitor-regular
                namespace: nvsentinel
              status:
                (numberReady < desiredNumberScheduled): true
        # Stale-rollout guard: numberReady alone can't distinguish a node
        # still running the previous revision's pod (also Ready) from a
        # fully current rollout. Flat (not status:-nested) so
        # metadata.generation is addressable below. updatedNumberScheduled
        # is itself omitempty (unlike desiredNumberScheduled/numberReady),
        # so it needs the `|| `0`` null-coalescing too.
        - error:
            resource:
              apiVersion: apps/v1
              kind: DaemonSet
              metadata:
                name: syslog-health-monitor-regular
                namespace: nvsentinel
              ((status.updatedNumberScheduled || `0`) < status.desiredNumberScheduled): true
        - error:
            resource:
              apiVersion: apps/v1
              kind: DaemonSet
              metadata:
                name: syslog-health-monitor-regular
                namespace: nvsentinel
              ((status.observedGeneration || `0`) < metadata.generation): true
        # nic-health-monitor: same negative form again. Its chart
        # condition (global.nicHealthMonitor.enabled) is off in every
        # recipe except those composing the nvsentinel-nic-health-monitor
        # mixin, so on the other platforms these four ops pass vacuously
        # on a 404 and only bite where the mixin is applied.
        - error:
            resource:
              apiVersion: apps/v1
              kind: DaemonSet
              metadata:
                name: nic-health-monitor
                namespace: nvsentinel
              status:
                (desiredNumberScheduled > `0`): false
        - error:
            resource:
              apiVersion: apps/v1
              kind: DaemonSet
              metadata:
                name: nic-health-monitor
                namespace: nvsentinel
              status:
                (numberReady < desiredNumberScheduled): true
        - error:
            resource:
              apiVersion: apps/v1
              kind: DaemonSet
              metadata:
                name: nic-health-monitor
                namespace: nvsentinel
              ((status.updatedNumberScheduled || `0`) < status.desiredNumberScheduled): true
        - error:
            resource:
              apiVersion: apps/v1
              kind: DaemonSet
              metadata:
                name: nic-health-monitor
                namespace: nvsentinel
              ((status.observedGeneration || `0`) < metadata.generation): true
    - name: validate-all-pods-healthy
      try:
        # Assert no pods are in unhealthy phases (Pending / Failed /
        # Unknown) or stuck in Running phase with a known-bad
        # container-waiting reason (CrashLoopBackOff,
        # ImagePullBackOff, ErrImagePull, CreateContainerConfigError).
        # Phase-only filtering misses CrashLoopBackOff because such
        # pods typically remain in Running phase with an unhealthy
        # container.
        - error:
            resource:
              apiVersion: v1
              kind: Pod
              metadata:
                namespace: nvsentinel
              status:
                phase: Pending
        - error:
            resource:
              apiVersion: v1
              kind: Pod
              metadata:
                namespace: nvsentinel
              status:
                phase: Failed
        - error:
            resource:
              apiVersion: v1
              kind: Pod
              metadata:
                namespace: nvsentinel
              status:
                phase: Unknown
        # JMESPath projection (not single-element match): kyverno-json's
        # sliceNode.Assert gates on exact slice length before per-element
        # comparison, so a `containerStatuses: - state: ...` shape only
        # matches single-container pods and silently passes sidecars. Use
        # `containerStatuses[?...] | length(@) > 0` to fire on any
        # container at any index. Parallel initContainerStatuses block
        # below catches init-container failures (invisible to
        # containerStatuses). Per PR #1245 review (@ArangoGutierrez).
        - error:
            resource:
              apiVersion: v1
              kind: Pod
              metadata:
                namespace: nvsentinel
              status:
                ((containerStatuses || `[]`)[?state.waiting.reason == 'CrashLoopBackOff' || state.waiting.reason == 'ImagePullBackOff' || state.waiting.reason == 'ErrImagePull' || state.waiting.reason == 'CreateContainerConfigError'] | length(@) > `0`): true
        - error:
            resource:
              apiVersion: v1
              kind: Pod
              metadata:
                namespace: nvsentinel
              status:
